I am a 32-year-old woman farmer in Dongfu village, Anzhai township, Quzhou County. I have no schooling, but I have been farming since I was a girl helping my parents, and I know this land well. My family has about 5 mu of irrigated flatland — not much, but enough to feed us and earn a little cash if we manage it right.

This year, like every year, I will grow the wheat-and-corn rotation. That is what everyone around here does. The winter wheat was sown last October and is greening up now; after we harvest it in early June, I will plant summer maize straight away without ploughing — we call it "no-tillage corn." I would not dream of leaving the land idle in summer; the soil is good and the water is there, so two crops in one year is the only sensible way.

For the wheat, I will rotary-till the field before sowing. I use improved wheat seed — about 30 jin per mu — either saved from last year or bought from the village supply shop if my own seed looks weak. I will apply basal compound fertilizer and top-dress with urea when the wheat joints, because that is when it gets hungry. I irrigate four times: the winter-irrigation, the green-up water, the jointing water, and the grain-filling water. We pump from the village well and flood the borders. I also spray pesticides about four times — herbicide once early, then insecticide and fungicide when I see aphids or rust appearing, which they always do.

For the maize, I will buy hybrid seed packets from the shop — one packet per mu — and drill them into the stubble right after the wheat comes out. No ploughing; the stubble protects the soil and saves me time and diesel. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat, just one basal dressing and maybe a side-dressing at the big-flare stage. I will irrigate twice, once if June is dry and again at flowering. Three pesticide sprays are usually enough for corn borers and weeds.

I do not grow cotton or vegetables. Cotton needs too much hand-picking and pruning, and vegetables are risky — prices crash overnight. Wheat and corn have steady buyers, and I can store them if the price is low. This is the safe path for a woman farming alone on 5 mu.
